author: rozaru
body:
I am doing the CC annotation for these 2 enzymes Alg7 and Alg13 which catalytic activities occur on the cytosolic face of the ER and Alg14 which acts as an adaptor to bring Alg13 to the ER membrane.


![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cbaf564b-a0d0-48ab-8b2f-4a4f89c8bb5d)

I am not that I understand the difference between these terms:

```
|__endoplasmic reticulum membrane 
 	|__cytoplasmic side of endoplasmic reticulum membrane part of
	|__extrinsic component of endoplasmic reticulum membrane] part of
```

> **cytoplasmic side of endoplasmic reticulum membrane**
> The side (leaflet) of the plasma membrane that faces the cytoplasm.

is this term meant to be used for membrane proteins whose function is localized on the cytosolic face of the ER?

> **extrinsic component of endoplasmic reticulum membrane**
> The component of the endoplasmic reticulum membrane consisting of gene products and protein complexes that are loosely bound to one of its surfaces, but not integrated into the hydrophobic region.
title: Difference between GO:0042406: extrinsic component of endoplasmic reticulum membrane and GO:0098554:cytoplasmic side of endoplasmic reticulum membrane

author: cmungall
body:
I agree it's not immediately obvious. The ontology should contain embedded images to illustrate these scenarios. (maybe we should take this to ontology tracker?)

It might help to look at the two is-a hierarchies, where the distinction is embedded/anchored vs loosely bound

## Side of membrane

* [] GO:0098552 ! side of membrane "A cellular component consisting of one leaflet of a membrane bilayer and any proteins embedded or anchored in it or attached to its surface."
    * [i] GO:0098576 ! lumenal side of membrane "Any side (leaflet) of a membrane that faces the lumen of an organelle."
        * [i] **GO:0098553 ! lumenal side of endoplasmic reticulum membrane "The side (leaflet) of the plasma membrane that faces the lumen."**
    * [i] GO:0098562 ! cytoplasmic side of membrane "The side of a membrane that faces the cytoplasm."
        * [i] **GO:0098554 ! cytoplasmic side of endoplasmic reticulum membrane "The side (leaflet) of the plasma membrane that faces the cytoplasm."**

## Extrinsic component

* [] GO:0019898 ! extrinsic component of membrane "The component of a membrane consisting of gene products and protein complexes that are loosely bound to one of its surfaces, but not integrated into the hydrophobic region."
    * [i] GO:0031312 ! extrinsic component of organelle membrane "The component of an organelle membrane consisting of gene products and protein complexes that are loosely bound to one of its surfaces, but not integrated into the hydrophobic region."
        * [i] **GO:0042406 ! extrinsic component of endoplasmic reticulum membrane "The component of the endoplasmic reticulum membrane consisting of gene products and protein complexes that are loosely bound to one of its surfaces, but not integrated into the hydrophobic region."**

author: deustp01
body:
> Side of membrane

A tangent here. For "lumenal side of membrane" applied to a cytoplasmic organelle, the membrane defines a closed three-dimensional space whose interior is the organelle lumen and whose exterior is the cytosol. That same geometry works at the level of the whole cell: the plasma membrane defines a closed three-dimensional space whose interior is the cytoplasm and whose exterior is the extracellular space. So in the ontology structure above, what is the correct logical relationship among the "side of membrane", "lumenal side of membrane", and "cytoplasmic side of membrane" terms? This is a question, not a stealth argument - it feels like something is not exactly right but I have no idea how to describe it better.
